clue.text: Dish requiring almost ten cents on total

indicators.note: almost means the word for ten cents loses its final letter

parts.note: a dime is the American ten-cent coin
a total is a sum

explanation.surface: A meal that costs barely more than ten cents on top of the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum is a Cantonese meal of small dumplings and similar bites, so it is a kind of dish.

clue.text: No man is troubled by one disorder

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of the three words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Every single person is troubled by one ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'No man is' as a sentence opening; it is just fodder, and 'troubled' makes NSOMNIA of it to follow the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia, chronic sleeplessness, is a medical disorder.

clue.text: Crossing to pay for game for four

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
bridge is a card game played by four people in two pairs

explanation.surface: A crossing whose fee is paid to play a four-handed game.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge is a crossing for pedestrians over a road, river or railway.

clue.text: Publicity in favour of movement

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
motion is movement

explanation.surface: Advertising that supports a cause or campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is advertising or publicity to boost sales or awareness.

clue.text: Eager to help, embracing victory

indicators.note: embracing means one word holds another inside its arms

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Keen to give assistance, now that the win is in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid is a synonym of keen or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Jack stole criminal's barge

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: criminal's reads as criminal is, so the letters of stole are crooked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Jack pinched a crook's canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal's' (criminal is) rearranges STOLE into OSTLE. 'barge' looks like a boat but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to push roughly through people, which is to jostle them.

clue.text: Turn stream, getting the effect of exposure

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle
burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: Diverting a brook, and suffering for being out in the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is skin reddened by exposure to the wind, a typical result of being outdoors in cold air.

clue.text: Like some rock genius confused about love?

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around another letter
confused means the letters of genius are muddled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A muddled genius wondering whether stone can feel affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes IGNEUS from GENIUS, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock forms from cooled magma, so the adjective describes some kinds of rock.

clue.text: Stop the flow of waste material

indicators.note: of means part of, so the answer comes from inside the following words

explanation.surface: An instruction to staunch the escape of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in waSTE Material; 'of' (part of) signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding or a leak is to stop its flow.

clue.text: Right — put vinegar initially into garlic sauce dish

indicators.note: into means one letter goes inside a word

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to add a splash of vinegar to garlic sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is an Italian pasta dish of stuffed parcels.

clue.text: Working mothers welcome right over a limited period

indicators.note: welcome means taking another piece in, as a host takes in a guest
working means the letters of mothers are worked into a different order

explanation.surface: Mothers with jobs greeting a man back in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a cricket over or a link, but belongs to the definition; 'Working' makes SHOTERM, which opens to welcome the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-term describes something lasting or concerned with only a brief time ahead.

clue.text: Old-fashioned fruit salad at last

parts.note: a date is a fruit of the palm

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word salad

explanation.surface: Fruit salad is finally recognised as a retro dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated looks old-fashioned or out of style.

clue.text: Scrooge has name for son becoming an underground worker

indicators.note: name for son means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: Ebenezer Scrooge, from Dickens, is the archetypal miser

explanation.surface: Scrooge renames his son, who goes off to work down a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner works below ground in a mine.

clue.text: Propose a posh but dramatic scene

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for discussion
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Putting forward a refined yet theatrical suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, often figures posed motionless on stage.

clue.text: Dog left in support with sentry

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed within a word

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a sentry is a guard

explanation.surface: A hound is placed at the rear beside a watchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog is an old insult for a scoundrel, and a blackguard is a contemptible rogue.

clue.text: Sabotage ruined men's pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words are trashed and reordered

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, giving men

explanation.surface: Ruined underwear belonging to men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is the anagram signal, British slang for rubbish, and rearranges RUINED MEN; it is not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine something is to weaken or sabotage it by stealth.

clue.text: Cheers up?

parts.note: cheering while risen to one's feet: applause given by an audience that has got up out of its seats

explanation.surface: Is someone being encouraged out of a low mood?
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences rise to applaud a great performance, a sign of the highest acclaim with cheers from people who are up.

clue.text: Questions factions grabbing American power

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for factions seizes other letters inside

parts.note: sects are factions
US is American

explanation.surface: Rival groups seizing control of American power.
explanation.definitionFit: To question a claim is to suspect it is untrue, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Firing favourite absent from planned petitioning

indicators.note: planned means the remaining letters are organised into a new order

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Dismissal of the boss's favourite cut from an organised petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absent from' takes PET away from PETITIONING; 'planned' rearranges the rest, ITIONING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the firing of fuel in an engine.

clue.text: Current boyfriend's crush

definitions.meaning: a current boyfriend or girlfriend, in informal speech
to crush is to press tightly

explanation.surface: My present boyfriend is my crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeeze is slang for a partner, and to squeeze is to crush.

clue.text: Source of pride in volte-face gives improvement in fortune

indicators.note: in means one letter goes inside a word

parts.note: a volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion, a U-turn

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word pride

explanation.surface: Swallowing one's pride and changing course turns luck around.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise, an improvement in circumstances or trade.

clue.text: In Scotland know why broadcast comes before a republic

parts.note: ken is Scots for know

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is said aloud on air

parts.note: the word why spoken

explanation.surface: A Scot asks why a broadcast promotes a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African republic.

clue.text: Not at home around city? No matter

indicators.note: around means the word goes round another

parts.note: away means not at home
NY is New York, the city

explanation.surface: Being away from home doesn't matter in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway means regardless or no matter.

clue.text: Corner section on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a section

explanation.surface: A section of road on an uphill bend.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap them.

clue.text: Praise luck turning on former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or luck

explanation.surface: Praising one's luck in moving on from an ex.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Look — a fellow with brains!

definitions.note: a singular head of brains, a noun matching

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Look at that bright, clever chap!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' means use your head: loaf of bread is Cockney rhyming slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaf is British slang for the head, hence intelligence or brains.

clue.text: Make an effort to follow brand in woodwork

indicators.note: to follow means the effort word comes after the brand word

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car
to try is to make an effort

explanation.surface: Push to keep up with a fashionable label in carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is decorative woodwork inlaid with veneers.

clue.text: Trainer's ground? Yes!

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters of trainer are milled into a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Is this the trainer's patch? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is both the anagram signal and the definition; the 'Yes!' confirms the whole clue reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is ground, the land a racehorse trainer might gallop over.

clue.text: Framework for flipping monster in most of drama

indicators.note: in means the flipped word sits within another
most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a monster

explanation.surface: Stage scaffolding for an upturned monster in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'flipping' gives ERGO, set inside PLA, which is the drama shortened by 'most of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework of posts and beams for climbing plants.
